issues.description: The `inject` function parameter typing is inconsistent across the exercise text and code. The problem statement specifies `inject(circ: stim.Circuit, data_qubit: int, injection_qubit) -> int` but uses `injection_qubit` as a qubit index (an int), while the template and solution leave `injection_qubit` untyped. This can confuse students about whether non-integer Stim targets are allowed, especially since other APIs in the same exercise type qubit indices as `int`.
issues.suggestedFix: Update the function signature in the template (and optionally the solution for consistency) to `def inject(circ: stim.Circuit, data_qubit: int, injection_qubit: int) -> int:`.

issues.description: The template’s return type annotation for `simulate_msd_one_round` conflicts with the specification and the solution. The problem statement requires `simulate_msd_one_round(...) -> tuple[float, float]` (error rate, acceptance rate) and the solution matches this, but the template declares `-> list[float]`, which misleads students and breaks type checking/intellisense for callers like `plot_msd` that treat the result as a 2-tuple.
issues.suggestedFix: Change the template signature to `def simulate_msd_one_round(n_shots: int, p: float) -> tuple[float, float]:`.

issues.description: The template docstring for `build_msd_circ` misdescribes the second returned list. The problem statement says the function must return measurement indices for (1) teleportation/injection measurements and (2) the destructive X-basis measurements of the 15 tetrahedral-code qubits (in qubit order). The template docstring instead describes the second list as indices of the “final X-basis measurements of the distilled state”, which is a different qubit/entity and can mislead students about what to pass into `detect_errors`.
issues.suggestedFix: Edit the `build_msd_circ` template docstring so the second list is described as “indices of the destructive X-basis measurements of the 15 tetrahedral-code qubits (in qubit order)” instead of measurements of the distilled state.
